profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Indeed
profile.summary:
I am working at Indeed helping protect our job seekers from fraudulent actors. I love helping people find jobs securely and reducing fraud in general.

I am truly passionate about programming and excited to build a career around something I enjoy so much.  It's my hobby as well as my job.  I frequently build home projects, compete in hackathons, join community events to learn new technologies, and volunteer for coding causes.

I have a BS in Computer Science from UT-Austin.

Old classmates, colleagues, and friends feel free to reach out to me.

positions.title: Cloud Competitive Analysis - Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software engineer for cloud competitive analysis team.  Our team's mission is to create a holistic view of the major cloud providers and supply feedback to internal teams on gaps and projected future states for the competitors.  We focus on the end users and work in the mindset of an end user choosing between IBM Cloud, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and others.

We consistently focus on coupling emerging technologies with existing cloud offerings and produce real world use cases with the intent of mirroring real life decision making from external customers, focusing on ease of use, quality of service, price, performance, and expected future state.

honors.title: 2016 Intel Joule Hackathon - 1st Place
honors.description:
The theme for the Joule Hackathon was to utilize the Intel Joule micro computer and Realsense 3D vision attachment.  Our team created a hat that would aid the visually impaired.  As you got close to an obstacle it would give off different buzzes (via micro vibration motors along the temples) to indicate direction and proximity.  It also had features to scan, OCR, auto-translate (if required), and read signs to the user via cloud connectivity.

It was also super stylish!
https://twitter.com/intel_stewart/status/797113396604780545

honors.title: 2016 Intel IoT Roadshow Hackathon - 3rd Place
honors.description:
The theme was to use the Intel Edison (small prototyping computer) to make an IoT device and application.  Our team made an IoT Pillbox with dispenser and accompanying web application.  The user's doctor or caregiver can create their medication schedule and set up the pillbox to dispense whichever type of medication they have.  The box is auto-dispensing, the user or caregiver can just dump the pills directly into each chamber.  When the scheduled time has come there is an audible and visual alert.  The user can press the button, receive their required dosage for that scheduled time, and the pillbox will automatically update our cloud backend.  If the user did not take their medicine on time the system will send a call or text reminder (number and choice adjusted on the app) and if they still don't take it after the reminder it calls or texts their caregiver to check up on them.  It also records history for the user's doctor.

3rd place winner
Best use of 3D printing winner

projects.title: Lithium
projects.description: A Java-based Lisp interpreter, using JavaCC to parse its inputs and instances of Visitor classes to process its parse tree. Grammar and all classes were written from scratch.

patents.title: Dynamically determining highlights of media content based on user interaction metrics and/or social media metric
patents.description: When determining which events to include in a highlight reel (such as during a sports game) we can also take secondary inputs directly from users. For example if more people rewind on a play, chat volume increases on the Twitch broadcast, or Twitter mentions about a player increase. These are all metrics that can be input to determine how 'exciting' a play was and may be a better method of capture than static metrics such as score or yards gained.

testScores.description: GRE for graduate school admissions.  When compared to the pool of GRE test takers: 89 percentile verbal, 98 percentile quantitative (perfect score), 93 percentile analytical writing.
